creatinine.name: Serum Creatinine
creatinine.description: Creatinine is a waste product produced primarily from normal muscle metabolism. It is filtered from the blood by the kidneys and is commonly measured as part of the assessment of kidney function.
creatinine.usedFor: Assessment of kidney function and estimation of glomerular filtration.
creatinine.educationalNote: Blood creatinine can be influenced by factors such as muscle mass, age, diet and hydration status and should not be interpreted in isolation.

glucose.name: Glucose
glucose.description: Glucose is the primary carbohydrate used by the body as an energy source. Blood glucose measurements are commonly used to evaluate glucose metabolism.
glucose.usedFor: Assessment of blood glucose levels and evaluation of disorders of glucose metabolism.
glucose.educationalNote: Glucose concentrations can vary depending on fasting status, meals, medications, stress and other physiological factors.

urea.name: Urea
urea.description: Urea is the major nitrogen-containing waste product formed in the liver during protein metabolism and is eliminated primarily through the kidneys.
urea.usedFor: Assessment of renal function and evaluation of nitrogen metabolism.
urea.educationalNote: Urea concentration can be affected by hydration, protein intake, renal function and other physiological conditions.

bun.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
bun.description: Blood Urea Nitrogen represents the amount of nitrogen present in the blood in the form of urea.
bun.usedFor: Assessment of renal function and evaluation of nitrogen balance.
bun.educationalNote: BUN and urea are related but are not numerically identical because BUN represents only the nitrogen component of urea.

uric_acid.name: Uric Acid
uric_acid.description: Uric acid is the final product of purine metabolism in humans and is primarily eliminated through the kidneys.
uric_acid.usedFor: Evaluation of uric acid metabolism and conditions associated with abnormal uric acid concentrations.
uric_acid.educationalNote: Uric acid concentration can be influenced by diet, renal excretion, medications and metabolic factors.

total_bilirubin.name: Total Bilirubin
total_bilirubin.description: Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced during the breakdown of heme, primarily from aging red blood cells.
total_bilirubin.usedFor: Evaluation of bilirubin metabolism and assessment of conditions affecting the liver, bile ducts or red blood cell breakdown.
total_bilirubin.educationalNote: Bilirubin interpretation generally considers total and direct fractions together with clinical findings and other laboratory results.

direct_bilirubin.name: Direct Bilirubin
direct_bilirubin.description: Direct bilirubin primarily represents conjugated bilirubin that has been processed by the liver and is more water-soluble.
direct_bilirubin.usedFor: Evaluation of bilirubin metabolism and hepatobiliary function.
direct_bilirubin.educationalNote: Direct bilirubin is generally interpreted together with total bilirubin and other liver-related laboratory parameters.

cholesterol.name: Total Cholesterol
cholesterol.description: Cholesterol is a lipid required for cell membranes, steroid hormones and bile acid production.
cholesterol.usedFor: Assessment of lipid status and cardiovascular risk as part of a lipid profile.
cholesterol.educationalNote: Total cholesterol is generally evaluated together with HDL, LDL, triglycerides and other clinical risk factors.

hdl.name: HDL Cholesterol
hdl.description: HDL cholesterol represents cholesterol carried in high-density lipoprotein particles.
hdl.usedFor: Evaluation of lipid status and cardiovascular risk.
hdl.educationalNote: HDL cholesterol is one component of a lipid profile and should be considered together with other lipid measurements and clinical risk factors.

ldl.name: LDL Cholesterol
ldl.description: LDL cholesterol represents cholesterol carried in low-density lipoprotein particles.
ldl.usedFor: Evaluation of lipid status and cardiovascular risk.
ldl.educationalNote: LDL cholesterol is commonly considered an important component of cardiovascular risk assessment.

triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
triglycerides.description: Triglycerides are a major form of fat stored and transported in the body and serve as an important energy source.
triglycerides.usedFor: Assessment of lipid metabolism and cardiovascular and metabolic risk.
triglycerides.educationalNote: Triglyceride concentrations can be influenced by recent food intake, alcohol consumption, metabolic factors and medications.

total_protein.name: Total Protein
total_protein.description: Total protein represents the combined concentration of major proteins present in a biological fluid, particularly albumin and globulins in serum.
total_protein.usedFor: Assessment of protein status and evaluation of various conditions affecting protein metabolism or distribution.
total_protein.educationalNote: Total protein should be interpreted together with albumin, globulin and other relevant laboratory findings.

albumin.name: Albumin
albumin.description: Albumin is the most abundant protein in plasma and is synthesized primarily by the liver. It contributes significantly to plasma oncotic pressure and transports various substances.
albumin.usedFor: Evaluation of protein status, liver-related conditions and other clinical conditions affecting albumin concentration.
albumin.educationalNote: Albumin concentration can be affected by nutritional status, fluid balance, liver function and other physiological factors.

calcium.name: Calcium
calcium.description: Calcium is an essential mineral involved in bone structure, muscle contraction, nerve transmission and several cellular processes.
calcium.usedFor: Evaluation of calcium metabolism and disorders affecting bone, parathyroid function and mineral balance.
calcium.educationalNote: Total calcium concentration can be influenced by albumin concentration, and interpretation may require consideration of other related measurements.

magnesium.name: Magnesium
magnesium.description: Magnesium is an essential electrolyte involved in numerous enzymatic reactions, neuromuscular function and cellular metabolism.
magnesium.usedFor: Evaluation of magnesium balance and disorders affecting electrolyte and mineral metabolism.
magnesium.educationalNote: Magnesium concentration may be affected by renal function, medications, gastrointestinal losses and other physiological factors.

phosphate.name: Phosphate
phosphate.description: Phosphate is an essential mineral involved in bone structure, energy metabolism, cellular signaling and nucleic acid synthesis.
phosphate.usedFor: Evaluation of mineral metabolism and conditions affecting renal, bone and parathyroid function.
phosphate.educationalNote: Phosphate concentration should generally be interpreted together with calcium and other relevant mineral metabolism measurements.

iron.name: Iron
iron.description: Iron is an essential mineral required for hemoglobin synthesis, oxygen transport and several metabolic processes.
iron.usedFor: Evaluation of iron status and investigation of disorders involving iron metabolism.
iron.educationalNote: Serum iron varies throughout the day and is generally interpreted together with other iron studies.

sodium.name: Sodium
sodium.description: Sodium is the major extracellular cation and plays an important role in fluid balance, nerve transmission and muscle function.
sodium.usedFor: Evaluation of electrolyte and fluid balance.
sodium.educationalNote: Sodium concentration is influenced by water balance and should be interpreted in the context of overall electrolyte and fluid status.

potassium.name: Potassium
potassium.description: Potassium is the major intracellular cation and is essential for normal nerve and muscle function, including cardiac electrical activity.
potassium.usedFor: Evaluation of electrolyte balance and monitoring conditions or treatments that affect potassium levels.
potassium.educationalNote: Potassium results can be affected by sample handling and hemolysis, so unexpected results may require laboratory verification.

chloride.name: Chloride
chloride.description: Chloride is a major extracellular anion that contributes to fluid balance and acid-base regulation.
chloride.usedFor: Evaluation of electrolyte and acid-base balance.
chloride.educationalNote: Chloride is generally interpreted together with sodium and other electrolyte measurements.

hemoglobin.name: Hemoglobin
hemoglobin.description: Hemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying protein found inside red blood cells.
hemoglobin.usedFor: Evaluation of oxygen-carrying capacity and assessment of anemia and other hematological conditions.
hemoglobin.educationalNote: Hemoglobin should be interpreted together with other complete blood count parameters and clinical findings.

hematocrit.name: Hematocrit
hematocrit.description: Hematocrit represents the proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells.
hematocrit.usedFor: Evaluation of red blood cell volume and assessment of anemia, erythrocytosis and related conditions.
hematocrit.educationalNote: Hematocrit is affected by red blood cell mass as well as plasma volume.

rbc.name: RBC Count
rbc.description: The red blood cell count represents the number of circulating red blood cells in a specified volume of blood.
rbc.usedFor: Evaluation of red blood cell production and disorders such as anemia and erythrocytosis.
rbc.educationalNote: RBC count is generally interpreted together with hemoglobin, hematocrit and red cell indices.

wbc.name: WBC Count
wbc.description: The white blood cell count represents the number of circulating leukocytes in a specified volume of blood.
wbc.usedFor: Evaluation of immune and inflammatory responses and various hematological conditions.
wbc.educationalNote: WBC count is usually interpreted together with the differential white blood cell count.

platelets.name: Platelet Count
platelets.description: Platelets are small cellular fragments that play an important role in primary hemostasis and blood clot formation.
platelets.usedFor: Evaluation of platelet number and assessment of bleeding or clotting-related conditions.
platelets.educationalNote: Platelet count should be interpreted together with clinical findings and other coagulation or hematology parameters.

urine_albumin.name: Urine Albumin
urine_albumin.description: Urine albumin measurement evaluates the amount of albumin excreted into urine and can provide information about kidney filtration barrier function.
urine_albumin.usedFor: Assessment of urinary albumin excretion and evaluation of kidney health.
urine_albumin.educationalNote: Urinary albumin may vary with hydration, exercise, infection and other factors. ACR is commonly used to account for urine concentration.

urine_protein.name: Urine Protein
urine_protein.description: Urine protein measurement evaluates the amount of protein present in urine and can provide information about renal and urinary tract conditions.
urine_protein.usedFor: Evaluation of urinary protein excretion and assessment of kidney-related conditions.
urine_protein.educationalNote: Urine protein concentration is influenced by urine dilution. Protein-to-creatinine ratio can help account for urine concentration.

urine_creatinine.name: Urine Creatinine
urine_creatinine.description: Urine creatinine measurement represents creatinine excreted into urine and is commonly used to account for urine concentration in ratio-based measurements.
urine_creatinine.usedFor: Calculation of urine ratios such as ACR and PCR and evaluation of urinary creatinine excretion.
urine_creatinine.educationalNote: Urine creatinine concentration varies with urine dilution and individual physiological factors.
